industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; medium conviction. Interpump (IP-IT) at EUR 36.0 (2026-09-29) is a cyclical recovery in a solid, cash-generative, decentralised industrial bought at a trough multiple; the 'Modal return' on the modal path is a C (about 17.6 percent a year over eighteen months, about 12.8 percent a year over three years at a blended 14.7x) against the 20 percent bar, and clears the bar only on the re-rating branch (15.6x) over eighteen months, which the record puts at probable, about 60 percent. The gate line does not park the case (no D or F on management, business quality, predictability or trackability, all B); the return does. Progress on either alone: a price at or below about EUR 33 (blended eighteen-month return about 25 percent a year, three-year about 16 percent), or FY2026 results (about February 2027) showing EPS at or above EUR 2.15 with no fourth-quarter cancellation wave, which would lift the re-rating odds toward 80 percent and the eighteen-month 'Modal return' toward a B. Bearish on a negative Hydraulics organic quarter, or trade working capital still at 40 percent of sales at year-end 2026.
case: - The change is external and cyclical: the mobile-hydraulics destocking cycle that ran seven quarters (averaging 12 percent contraction) has ended. Hydraulics grew +2.2 percent organically in Q1 2026 and +6.2 percent in Q2 2026; margin +30 basis points to 21.2 percent while absorbing acquired perimeters; utilisation at Walvoil and White Drive about 95 percent; book-to-bill above 1.0 in both divisions; dealer inventories 1.2 months by March 2026 from 2.8. Construction and earthmoving up double-digit (infrastructure and data-centre investment), trucks stabilised and grew, agriculture still deteriorating; North America up mid-teens, Far East high-single-digit, Latin America significantly down. Group organic only +0.7 percent in H1 2026 because Water Jetting laps the H1 2025 Hammelmann order. Own cycle B; demand C; macro D (German sales -5 percent, French -3 percent in 2025; Middle East delays; stronger euro, 5 percent appreciation worth EUR 0.025 of EPS, about 1.3 percent); competition, disruption, political, supply side C. No force meets the 'Demand Inflection' test: backlog EUR 600m to EUR 700m, visibility under a year.

- The internal change is continuity: same founder, chief executive, bolt-on model, margin floor. Strong: acquisitions B (EUR 42m in 2026 for Padoan, MVV, Teknoice; 5.4x EBITDA average against a listed sector median of 13.8x; 50 to 60 percent sourced bilaterally; pipeline 10 to 20 targets; about 2.5 percent of FY2026 sales); shareholder returns B (buybacks EUR 47.8m H1 2026 against EUR 16.59m in 2025 and EUR 10.34m in 2024; authorisation to EUR 65.00 a share). Balance sheet C (net financial position to zero by 2028, transformative optionality mooted); strategy C (a larger transaction actively explored, weighting toward flow handling and food processing); standards C (trade working capital target 35 to 36 percent of sales from about 40 percent; capex about 4 percent); new products C; new geographies C (Walvoil China capacity doubling); price rises C (nominal pass-through, pricing about 0 percent in 2024); guidance D (reiterated, verbal steer only); chief executive D; other leaders D; perimeter reduction D. Rule of three not met; 'Change Forces' C.

- The chain has travelled all six layers for the near term: actions (pass-through, utilisation, buybacks), key operating metrics (four quarters of Hydraulics growth), financial statements (Q2 2026 EPS +8.2 percent), sell-side FY2026 estimates (+8.2 percent over three months). Not the multiple (13.4x, 6th percentile of five years); not the mid-term estimates in size (FY2027 +8.0 percent over three months, -2.0 over twelve).
counter_case: - At its strongest: Interpump is a value trap in a founder's twilight, and the current print is a restock. The shares are at a trough multiple because the market has concluded, correctly, that a decentralised acquirer of niche machinery businesses whose EPS has not grown in six years (EUR 1.70 in FY2019 to EUR 1.96 in FY2025), whose return on capital employed has fallen to 13.5 percent, whose larger division is structurally cyclical and whose smaller, higher-margin division now faces low-cost entry against a 40 percent price premium, deserves a low-teens multiple, and every cyclical upturn will be sold into until succession is resolved and organic growth is shown to exceed low-single-digit through a cycle.

- The +6.2 percent Hydraulics print, book-to-bill above 1.0 and EUR 716.8m of inventories are consistent with dealer double-ordering after a destocking phase rather than end demand; the risks research's analysis of competing hypotheses names the false-friend profile the winner with zero hard inconsistencies against the current metrics, so the metrics the case relies on for the clearing are the same metrics a restock would show, and the record concedes it cannot distinguish them until the fourth quarter reports. Management acknowledged material Q4 order cancellations and postponements in Hydraulics in each of the last three fiscal years; agriculture is still going down; net working capital at 44.2 percent of last-twelve-month revenue is the highest in eleven quarters. On this reading the recovery reverses in Q4 2026, the FY2027 consensus of EUR 2.46 to EUR 2.54 is cut, EPS stalls near EUR 2.1 to EUR 2.2, the multiple stays at its trough, and the return is the 1 percent dividend yield plus whatever buybacks add.
triggers: - Progress, either alone: price at or below about EUR 33 (blended eighteen-month return about 25 percent a year, three-year about 16 percent); or FY2026 results (about February 2027) with EPS at or above EUR 2.15 on the brokers' basis and no fourth-quarter cancellation wave (re-rating odds toward 80 percent; eighteen-month 'Modal return' toward B).
- Bearish: a negative Hydraulics organic quarter; trade working capital still at 40 percent of sales at year-end 2026.
- Hydraulics organic growth: Alarm below +2 percent in a quarter; Invalidate a negative quarter. Modal: mid-single-digit through FY2027.

- Group EBITDA margin: Alarm below 21.5 percent in a half-year; Invalidate below 22.0 percent for a full year. Modal: 22.1, 22.6, 22.8 percent FY2026 to FY2028 against guidance 22.0 to 22.5 percent and consensus 22.1, 22.7, 23.1.
- Re-rating: Alarm consensus FY2027 mean EPS below EUR 2.50 after the FY2026 results; Invalidate FY2026 EPS below EUR 2.10 on the brokers' basis. Modal 15.6x on the branch, 14.7x blended.
- Fourth-quarter pattern: Alarm any disclosed cancellations at Q4 2026; Invalidate Q4 2026 Hydraulics organic growth negative. Modal: a milder year-end destocking, as management expects.
